## Introduction

This week will introduce data types and key metrics for describing and representing data.

## Learning Objectives

By the end of this week, you will be able to:

1. Understand data types for quantitative research.
2. Describe and represent data using key metrics.
3. Visualise data with boxplot.

## Practical

To access the practical:

1. You can [preview](EDA1_practical.html) the practical - which includes the code in both R and Python.
2. You can [download](https://github.com/Bea-Taylor/Quant_Methods/tree/main/practicals) the practical here as a python notebook (.ipynb) - ready for you to run the code yourself.

:::{.callout-note}

To save a copy of notebook to your own GitHub Repo: follow the GitHub link, click on `Raw` and then `Save File As...` to save it to your own computer. Make sure to change the extension from `.ipynb.txt` (which will probably be the default) to `.ipynb`before adding the file to *your* GitHub repository.

:::
